texts.preamble: Mahesh Kumar vs Renu on 18 July, 2024 In The Court Of Sh. Jitendra Singh : Additional Sessions Judge (Electricity), North-West District Rohini Courts, Delhi In The Matter Of:- Cnr No. Dlnw01-011258-2023 Ca No. 271/2023 Shri Mahesh Kashyap Son of Late Shri Chhote Lal R/o H.No.D-1/31-32, 2nd Floor, Sector-11, Rohini, Delhi-110085. .... Appellant Versus Smt. Renu Daughter of Shri Dharamveer Resident of A-656, Shyam Colony, Budh Vihar Phase-2, Delhi-110086. ...Respondent Date of Institution : 11.12.2023 Date of Reserving judgment : 08.07.2024 Date of judgment : 18.07.2024 Judgment 1. Vide this order, I shall dispose of the appeal filed under Section 29 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (hereinafter referred to as 'D.V. Act') against the judgment dated Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.1 of 18 24.07.2023 (hereinafter referred to as 'impugned judgment') passed by Ld. MM, Mahila Court-01, North-West, Rohini Courts, Delhi in CC no.450/4/2023 (New No.4999/2016), titled as Renu vs. Mahesh Kumar under Section 12 of the PWDV Act whereby the application filed by the respondent/ wife (hereinafter referred to as "complainant") under Sec. 12 of PWDV Act has been partly allowed against the appellant/husband ( hereinafter referred to as "respondent"). 2.
texts.facts: Respondent filed WS wherein he denied the factum of marriage and all the allegations levelled by complainant against him. As per rules, it is the obligation of the hospital to convey the names of the parents with date of birth of the child as per their record but the said date of birth certificate shows a different picture and creates a grave suspicion about the manipulation of record. The respondent is already a married person since 24.05.1991 with Smt. Meera, d/o Sh. Sukhnandan Pardesi and that the Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate the evidences such as the marriage card, few photographs of marriage of respondent with complainant, Aadhar card and voter card of the wife of the respondent which sufficiently establish the existence of marriage of the respondent with Smt. Meera.
texts.arguments: As per Sec. 7(2) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, a marriage is deemed to be completed and binding when the rites and ceremonies include 'Saptapadi" are performed. The wife of respondent is still alive and has been staying with the respondent ever since the date of marriage and in view of the subsistence of earlier marriage of the respondent, no valid Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.4 of 18 marriage could have taken place between the respondent and the complainant and therefore, the case of the complainant is completely false, baseless, concocted and without any substance. The Ld. Counsel has relied upon the following judgments:- (i) Sneha Ahuja Vs. Satish Chander Ahuja and another, 2021 SCC OnLine Del 4984: (2022) 1 RCR ( Civil) 234. (ii) C.L. Jain Vs. Raghubir Singh, 2012 SCC OnLine Del 1556. (iii) Dolly Rani Vs. Manish Kumar Chanchal, 2024 INSC 355. (iv) Ram Sarup Gupta Vs. Bishun Narain Inter College, (1987) 2 SCC. (v) National Textile Corporation Ltd. Vs. Nareshkumar Badrikumar Jagad, (2011) 12 SCC 695. It is prayed that the present appeal may be allowed. (iii) Union of India Versus National Project Construction Corp. Ltd. (iv) M/s. Gautam Associates Versus Food Corporation of India. (v) Chanmuniyat(s) Versus Virendra Kumar Singh Kushwaha & Anr. (vi) Badshah Versus Sou. Urmila Badshah Godse & Anr. (vii) Shhailesh Bopche Versus Anita Bapche.

11. After analyzing the relevant provisions of the D.V. Act, it is culled out that the complainant can get relief under the said Act only when she qualifies to be a aggrieved person.
The expression "aggrieved person" means a woman who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the respondent and has been subjected to any act of domestic violence by the respondent.

The expression "domestic relationship"
means a relationship between two persons who live or have, at any point of time,
lived together in a shared household.

The relationship may be by : (i) consanguinity,
(ii) marriage or, (iii) through a relationship in the nature of a marriage, (iv) adoption or, (v) are family members living together as a joint family.
The expression "domestic relationship" is a comprehensive as well as expansive one.

If aggrieved person is living or at any point of time lived together in "shared household" with the person against whom allegations of domestic violence have been made, the Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.9 of 18 provisions of D.V. Act woul

It is relevant to note the expression "marriage" also encompasses "relationship in the nature of marriage".
12.

For seeking relief under the D.V. Act, in the case of relationship in the nature of marriage, the pre condition is that the allegation of domestic violence must relate to the period of subsistence of relationship in the nature of marriage.

13. From the pleadings and the documents, it is the case of the complainant that she got married with the respondent who is resident of H.No.D 1/31-32, Block-D, PKT-1, Sec. 11, Rohini, Delhi on 15.06.2009 at Haridwar.
The complainant and the respondent started residing at B- 55, Mange Ram Park, Budh Vihar, Phase-I, Delhi-86.
A girl child was borne out of the said wedlock on 18.12.2010.
As the complainant was subjected to domestic violence she left the shared household and shifted to her parental home.

The respondent has even denied that he lived in the shared household with the respondent.

The relationship by way of marriage or Relationship in the nature of marriage :-
20.
The factum of marriage has been categorically denied by the respondent.
The D.V. Act has to be interpreted in a manner to effectuate the very purpose and object of the Act.
For seeking relief under the D.V. Act, the complainant can not be expected to strictly prove all the ingredients of marriage.
Any other interpretation would defeat the Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.14 of 18 purpose of the Act.

The complainant has brought on record the Birth Certificate of her minor daughter as Ex.CW1/G wherein the name of the father has been mentioned as 'Mahesh Kashyap' and the address has been mentioned as B-55, Mange Ram Park, Delhi.
This is the same address on which the complainant has alleged that they lived as husband and wife.

Even otherwise, the complainant can seek relief under the D.V. Act if she is able to establish that the relationship between the complainant and the respondent was in the nature of marriage.
